mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as higher borrowing costs reduce corporate investments and consumer spending.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of overall economic growth, thus driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods with sustained HOUST increases, or if the correlation between HOUST growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which leads to increased wages and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE decreases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals increased economic activity, which is a positive indicator for corporate earnings and thus drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over a 3-month period, it indicates real demand growth, which is a positive signal for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > CPIAUCSL growth over 3 months
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the interaction effect between RSAFS and CPIAUCSL growth is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a 3-month period signals a strengthening labor market, which is a positive indicator for economic growth and thus drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases & UNRATE decreases over 3 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the interaction effect between PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a tightening monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as higher borrowing costs reduce corporate investments and consumer spending.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the periods with sustained FEDFUNDS increases, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) decreases by more than 1% in a month, it signals a contraction in economic activity, which is a negative indicator for corporate earnings and thus drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
